actions: Inspected OpenProver public ProofNet harness and run-inspection/logging code at pinned public master commit.
Verified the typed OpenProver planner action vocabulary and per-call token/time/cost archive fields.
Verified that public runs/ are gitignored and the ProofNet aggregate does not expose planner-action frequency/tool counts.
Verified Meta-Reasoner ACL 2026 CMAB mechanism and controlled progress-report/direct-selection/dynamic-arm ablations.
Verified 2026-08-20 Learning When to Think first-token NoThink/Short/Long compute allocation result.
Verified Search as Computation Allocation VOC-vs-information result.
Continued targeted search for direct Lean learned heterogeneous planner-level policy; no primary direct match surfaced in this pass.
key_new_findings: OpenProver already logs enough typed step/cost/outcome structure to build an offline heterogeneous-controller dataset, but evaluated raw ProofNet run trajectories are not released in the repository and likely require rerun or a separate artifact.
Meta-Reasoner gives non-Lean controlled evidence that compact progress state plus contextual-bandit strategy choice outperforms raw full-history context and direct LLM strategy selection.
Learning When to Think demonstrates learned discrete compute purchase with 41% lower mean MATH500 output length at near-base accuracy, but only as a trajectory-start action.
VOC theory implies formal-agent action routing should optimize expected terminal decision improvement net of action-specific cost rather than uncertainty/information gain alone.
exact_next_action: Specify a deterministic OpenProver event schema linking typed planner action to worker/tool/Lean result, action-specific cost, and next compact state; then search once for a public runs archive before moving to conservative offline contextual-bandit/off-policy evaluation and mid-trajectory compute-purchase methods.
